prompt.total_and_side: Put all {n} into {d} equal rows. How many in each row?
prompt.two_divisions: Which pair of sentences does this array show?
prompt.partial_row: Make rows of {d}. How many full rows can you make?

refusals.wrong-row-count: Make the number of rows the question asked for.
refusals.not-all-placed: Every one of them has to go into the array.
refusals.rows-unequal: The rows are not all the same length.

array.title: The Array Knows

hint.side1: The question wants {d} rows, all the same length.
hint.side2: Add rows until you have that many, then share the counters between them.
hint.side3: Now count along one row. That is the answer.
hint.pair1: Count the rows, then count along one row.
hint.pair2: One sentence divides by the rows. The other divides by the length of a row.
hint.pair3: Read both halves of every pair before you choose. The second half is where they differ.
hint.partial3: The short row at the end is what is left over. It is not a row.

array.onlyFull: Count only the rows that are completely full.

printed.pair: This array has {d} rows of {q}. Write both divisions it shows.
printed.partial: Put all {n} into rows of {d}. How many full rows, and how many left?

method.partial1: Draw rows of the size the question names, filling each before starting the next.
method.partial3: The short row at the end is what is left over.
method.side1: Make the number of rows the question asks for.
method.side2: Share the counters between them so the rows are all the same length.

refusals.more-fits: Another whole one still fits. Keep taking them away.
refusals.too-many-steps: That works, but it took too many goes. Undo some and take bigger chunks.
refusals.overshot: You have taken away more than there was. Undo the last one.

chunk.title: Take Away Chunks

hint.big1: Start with the biggest chunk you are sure of. Ten lots of {d} is {ten}.
hint.big2: Would twenty lots fit? That is {twenty}.
hint.big3: You can get there in {goes} goes. Take the big one first.
hint.lots1: Every chunk takes away some whole lots of {d}.
hint.lots2: Ten lots of {d} is {ten}. Start there if it fits.
hint.lots3: Stop when what is left is smaller than {d}.

chunk.printed: take away lots of {d} and keep a tally
chunk.method1: Take away a lot you are sure of — ten of them is always easy to work out.
chunk.method2: Write down how many lots you took, and carry on with what is left.
chunk.method3: Stop when what is left is too small for another lot. Add up your lots.

refusals.too-big: That is more than there is. Try a smaller digit.
refusals.too-small: Another whole one still fits there. Try a bigger digit.

column.title: The Written Method

hint.exact1: Start at the left. Division is the method that begins big.
hint.exact2: Each digit of {n} divides by {d} exactly, so every column gives a clean answer.
hint.exact3: One column at a time, rightwards. Every digit gets an answer above.
hint.exchange1: Start at the left. How many {d}s fit into {first}?
hint.exchange2: It will not go evenly. Write what is left small, in front of the next digit.
hint.exchange3: Then divide that whole new number — the small carry and the digit read together.
hint.remainder1: Start at the left and carry leftovers along as usual.
hint.remainder2: Keep going all the way to the last digit.
hint.remainder3: Nothing left to carry into, so what remains is the remainder.
hint.zero1: Take the places one at a time. Never skip a small-looking one.
hint.zero2: When {d} will not go into a place, that place gets zero.
hint.zero3: A zero above the line holds the place. Leaving it out shrinks the answer.
hint.long1: {d} will not fit one digit, so take two together.
hint.long2: Guess how many {d}s fit, then multiply your guess out to check it.
hint.longRemainder3: Too much left, guess bigger. What is left at the end is the remainder.
hint.longExact3: Too much left, guess bigger. Gone past, guess smaller.
hint.decimal1: Work out the whole part first, and see what is left.
hint.decimal2: Point after the answer, zero after the total, then carry on.
hint.decimal3: What was left becomes tenths, then hundredths. Nothing about the method changes at the point.

column.checkRemainder: The digits above the line are right. Check what is left at the end.
column.workBack: Work back along the places and check each one.
column.somethingLeft: Something is left over — check your digits.

method.decimal1: Divide the whole part first and see what is left.
method.decimal2: Put a point in the answer, and a zero after the total.
method.decimal3: Carry on exactly as before: what was left becomes tenths.
method.long1: Guess how many fit into the first part, then check by multiplying.
method.long2: Take it away, and bring the next digit down.
method.long3: Keep going to the last digit. What is left at the end is the remainder.
method.short1: Start at the left-hand digit and work right.
method.short2: Write what is left over small, in front of the next digit.
method.short3: Every place gets a digit above the line, even when that digit is zero.

prompt.reasonable: Somebody says {n} ÷ {d} = {claim}. Could that be right?

estimate.title: About How Much?

hint.compatible1: Leave the {d} alone. Move the big number instead.
hint.compatible2: Find a number near {n} that {d} goes into exactly.
hint.compatible3: Take the one that is easiest to divide, not the one that is nearest.
hint.reasonable1: Do not work it out. Just think about how big the answer should be.
hint.reasonable3: An answer ten times too big or too small is the commonest slip there is.
hint.check1: To check a division, multiply back.
hint.check2: Your answer, times the number you divided by, should give the total back.
hint.check3: If there was a remainder, add it on at the end.

estimate.easier: {total} works too, but {best} is easier to divide by {d}.

fault.right: It is about the right size.
fault.tooBig: Ten times too big — a digit has ended up in the wrong column.
fault.tooSmall: Ten times too small — a place has been lost.
fault.droppedZero: A zero has been dropped out of the middle.

estimate.multiplyBack: Multiply your answer by the number you divided by.
estimate.whichTotal: Which total is easier to divide by {d}?
estimate.printedClaim: Somebody says {n} ÷ {d} = {claim}. Could that be right?   yes / no
estimate.printedCheck: {n} ÷ {d} = {q}. Write the sum that checks it.
estimate.printedCheckRemainder: {n} ÷ {d} = {q} r {r}. Write the sum that checks it.
estimate.method1: Leave the number you are dividing by alone, and move the total instead.
estimate.method2: Divide that instead. The answer is about right.
estimate.method3: To check a division for real, multiply the answer back and add any remainder.

evidence.evenAndSum: {value} is even: {even}. Its digits add to {sum}.

prompt.factor_pairs: Find every number that divides into {value} exactly.
prompt.common_factors: Which numbers divide into both {value} and {other}?
prompt.prime_factors: Break {value} apart until only primes are left.

factors.title: Does It Go?

hint.last1: You do not need to divide. Look at the last digit.
hint.last2: Even last digits mean it divides by 2.
hint.last5: A last digit of 0 or 5 means it divides by 5.
hint.last10: Only a last digit of 0 means it divides by 10.
hint.sum3: If that total divides by 3, so does the whole number.
hint.sum9: If that total divides by 9, so does the whole number.
hint.four1: Look at just the last two digits.
hint.six1: Test it twice: by 2, and by 3.
hint.four2: If those two digits make a number that divides by 4, the whole thing does.
hint.six2: A number divides by 6 only if it divides by both 2 and 3.
hint.pairs1: Try dividing by 1, then 2, then 3, and so on.
hint.pairs2: Every time one goes exactly, you have found a pair — that number and its partner.
hint.pairs3: You can stop at {stop}. Past there you only meet the partners again.
hint.common1: A number has to divide into both, not just one.
hint.common2: Test each candidate against both numbers before you tap it.
hint.prime1: Split it into any two numbers that multiply to make it.
hint.prime2: Keep splitting the parts that can still be split.
hint.prime3: A prime cannot be split. When they are all prime, you are finished.

factors.notExact: {value} does not go exactly. Check it again.

stillToFind.one: There is one still to find.

factors.keepSplitting: Keep splitting until nothing can be split.
factors.nothingNewPast: Nothing new past {stop} — after that you only meet the partners again.

printed.common: Write every number that divides into both {value} and {other}.
printed.prime: Write {value} as a product of primes.
printed.divides: Does {tester} divide into {value} exactly?   yes / no

method.last2: Even means 2. A 0 or 5 means 5. Only a 0 means 10.
method.sum2: If that total divides by 3 or 9, so does the whole number.
method.combined1: For 4, look at the last two digits.
method.combined2: For 6, test by 2 and by 3. Both have to pass.
method.pairs1: Divide by 1, then 2, then 3, and keep going.
method.pairs2: Each one that goes exactly gives you a pair.
method.pairs3: Stop where the two halves of a pair meet.
method.common1: Find the factors of the first number.
method.common2: Keep only the ones that divide the second as well.
method.prime1: Split the number into two factors.
method.prime2: Keep splitting until every part is prime.

prompt.family: Which of these are true for {d}, {q} and {n}?
prompt.table_divide: Find {n} in the {d} row. Which column is it in?

facts.title: Facts You Know

hint.family1: Three numbers make four true sentences — two multiplications and two divisions.
hint.family2: {n} stands alone in the times facts, and leads the divides.
hint.table1: Run along the {d} row until you find {n}.
hint.table2: The column it is sitting in is the answer.
hint.missing1: The two questions on the card are the same question.
hint.missing2: Whatever fills the gap in {d} × ? = {n} is the answer to the division.
hint.halve8: Dividing by 8 is halving three times.
hint.halve2: Do one halving at a time and write down what you get.
hint.known1: Which multiplication would give you this total?
hint.known2: You want one whose answer is {n}, with a {d} in it.
hint.ask2: Count up in {d}s if you need to. You want to land on {n}.
hint.underTen: Ten {d}s is {ten}, so the answer is under ten.
hint.overTen: Ten {d}s is {ten}, so the answer is over ten.

facts.allFour: All four, and only those four.
facts.exactlyFour: There are exactly four true ones. Check each again.

printed.family: Write the four facts that use {d}, {q} and {n}.
printed.table: Find {n} in the {d} times table. Which column is it in?

method.family1: The biggest of the three numbers is the total.
method.family2: The other two multiply to make it, in either order.
method.family3: The total divided by one of them gives the other.
method.table1: Run along the row until you find the total.
method.table2: Read the column number above it.
method.halve2: Halve it again — and once more if you are dividing by 8.
method.fact1: Ask what the number you are dividing by, times something, makes the total.
method.fact2: The number that fills that gap is the answer.

prompt.back_to_zero: Start at {n} and hop back {d} at a time. How many hops to reach 0?
prompt.count_hops: These hops are {d} each. How many hops are there?
prompt.forward_to_total: Count up from 0 in {d}s. How many hops to reach {n}?

refusals.not-finished: Keep hopping until you get all the way there.
refusals.overshot: That is too far. Come back one hop.

line.title: Hop Back

hint.back2: Keep hopping until the marker is sitting on 0. Do not stop part way.
hint.back3: Now count the hops you made — not the numbers you landed on.
hint.count1: Count the arrows, not the numbers under them.
hint.count2: Where you finished is not the answer. How many jumps it took is.

line.landOnTotal: Stop when you land exactly on the total.
line.countedOn: The answer is how many times you counted on.
line.landedOn: That is a number you landed on. The answer is how many hops it took.

printed.count: Each hop is {d}. How many hops are drawn?
printed.forward: Count on from 0 in {d}s to {n}. How many hops?

line.figureLabel: Number line from 0 to {n} in steps of {d}

method.back1: Start at the total and jump back by the same amount each time.
method.back2: Keep going until you land exactly on zero.
method.back3: Count the jumps, not the numbers you land on.
method.forward1: Start at zero and count on by the same amount each time.

prompt.tens_quotient: {n} ÷ {d}. How many tens is that, and how many altogether?
prompt.split_exchange: {n} ÷ {d}. The tens will not divide on their own.

place.title: Place by Place

hint.tens2: Share {tens} tens between {d}. How many tens each?
hint.tens3: Then say how many that is altogether.
hint.scale1: Dividing by {d} asks how many {d}s are inside.
hint.scale2: Every digit moves one place to the right for a ten, two for a hundred.
hint.scale3: The digits move a place right. The zero goes because nothing holds it.
hint.tensTens1: Both numbers are a whole number of tens.
hint.tensTens2: {a} tens divided by {b} tens is just {a} ÷ {b}.
hint.tensTens3: The tens on each side cancel out.
hint.split2: Divide each part by {d} on its own.
hint.split3: Add what you get. That is the answer.
hint.exchange1: Try splitting {n} by its digits. Does each part divide by {d}?
hint.exchange2: It does not — so take the biggest lot of {d} tens that fits instead.
hint.exchange3: {parts} both divide by {d}. That is the split you want.

place.partWrong: The total is right, but one of the parts is not.
place.checkParts: Check each part on its own first.
place.eachPlace: Each place divides on its own.
place.digitsDoNot: The digits do not split here. {parts} do.

method.split1: Split the total into parts that each divide exactly.
method.split2: Divide each part on its own.
method.tens1: Read the total as a number of tens or hundreds.
method.tens2: Divide those, then say what it is altogether.

bus.setup: {total} children are going on a trip. Each bus holds {size}.

ask.round-up: How many buses are needed so that everybody goes?
ask.round-down: How many buses will be completely full?
ask.the-remainder: How many children are left after the full buses have gone?
ask.both: How many full buses, and how many children left over?

egg.setup: {total} eggs are being packed into boxes of {size}.

ask.round-up: How many boxes are needed to hold every egg?
ask.round-down: How many boxes can be filled completely?
ask.the-remainder: How many eggs will not fit into a full box?
ask.both: How many full boxes, and how many eggs left over?

ask.round-up: How many would each need if every pencil had to go to somebody?
ask.round-down: How many pencils does each child get?
ask.the-remainder: How many pencils are left over?
ask.both: How many each, and how many left over?

refusals.remainder-too-big: The leftover has to be smaller than the number you are dividing by.

remainder.title: What Is Left

hint.record2: Take those away. What is left is the remainder.
hint.record3: The remainder is always smaller than {d}.
hint.tooBig1: Look at the leftover. Could another whole group still come out of it?
hint.tooBig2: If the leftover is {d} or more, one more group fits.
hint.tooBig3: Move the extra groups across, and the answer fixes itself.
hint.form1: Work the division out first. Then read the question again.
hint.form2: Does the question want the full ones, one more, what is left, or both?
hint.story1: Do the division. Then decide which part of it the question wants.
hint.roundUp: Nobody can be left behind, so the leftover still needs one of its own.
hint.theRemainder: The question is about what did not fit.
hint.roundDown: The question is about the ones that are complete.

remainder.pairWrong: Check how many whole {d}s fit first.
remainder.asked: That is what the question asked for.
remainder.oneMore: That many would leave some behind. One more is needed.
remainder.readAgain: Read the question once more. Which part of the answer does it want?
remainder.optionRight: That is the one the question wants.
remainder.optionWrong: Which part of the answer was asked for?
remainder.printedWrong: Somebody wrote {n} ÷ {d} = {q} r {r}. Write it properly.
remainder.method1: Work out how many whole groups fit.
remainder.method2: What is left over is the remainder, and it is always smaller than the number you divided by.
remainder.method3: Read the question again to see which part of the answer it wants.

story.size_unknown: {who} has {whole} {thing} to share equally between {parts} friends.
story.remainder_context: {whole} {thing} are being put into boxes of {size}.
story.multi_step: {who} has {whole} {thing}. After keeping {extra}, the rest are shared equally between {parts} friends.

ask.eachFriend: How many does each friend get?
ask.boxesNeeded: How many boxes are needed so that none are left out?
ask.boxesFull: How many boxes can be filled completely?
ask.oneBox: How many are in one box?
ask.timesAsMany: How many times as many does {who} have?
ask.eachDay: If the days had all been the same, how many would that be each day?

story.title: In Words

hint.size1: The story tells you how many people are sharing.
hint.size2: Cut the bar into that many equal parts.
hint.size3: One of those parts is the answer.
hint.count1: The story tells you how big each bag is, not how many bags.
hint.count2: Ask how many of that size fit into the total.
hint.rem1: Divide first, and see what is left.
hint.rem2: Now read the question: does it want the full ones, or does everything have to fit?
hint.rate1: Every box holds the same amount.
hint.rate2: Share the total between the boxes to find what one holds.
hint.times1: This is not asking how many more.
hint.times2: It is asking how many of the smaller amount fit into the bigger one.
hint.times3: Try it: how many lots of the small number make the big one?
hint.multi1: There are two things to do, and the order matters.
hint.multi3: Only then share out what is left.
hint.mean1: Imagine the days were all the same.
hint.mean2: Add every day together, then share the total between the days.

story.keptBackFirst: Take away what is kept back first.
story.cutFirst: Cut the bar into the right number of parts first.
story.asked: That is what the story asked for.
story.howManyMore: That is how many MORE. The question asks how many TIMES as many.
story.readAgain: Read the story once more, slowly.

method.times1: Draw both amounts as bars, one under the other.
method.times2: Ask how many of the short bar fit along the long one.
method.times3: That is how many times as many — not the difference.
method.multi1: Read the whole story before writing anything.
method.multi3: Then share out what is left.
method.mean2: Share the total between however many values there were.
method.bar1: Draw the total as one bar.
method.bar2: Cut it into the parts the story describes.
method.bar3: One part, or the number of parts, is the answer.

prompt.share: Share all {n} between the {d} plates. How many on each?
prompt.shareHolders: Share all {n} between the {d} holders. How many on each?
prompt.group_by_size: Make groups of {d}. How many groups can you make?
prompt.which_meaning: What is this question asking for?
prompt.onePlate: Put all {n} onto the 1 plate. How many are on it?
prompt.nothingToShare: There is nothing to share. How many does each of the {d} plates get?
prompt.see_leftover: Share as many as you can between the {d} plates. How many on each?

refusals.not-equal: Every plate needs the same number.
refusals.another-group-fits: There are still enough left to make another group.
refusals.plate-not-full: Fill every group before you count them.
refusals.another-round-fits: There are still enough left to give one more to every plate.

hint.share2: One to each plate, then round again, until the pile is empty.
hint.share3: When the pile is empty, count what is on just one plate. That is the answer.
hint.halve1: Halving means sharing between exactly two. There are always two plates.
hint.halve2: One to this plate, one to that one, over and over, until the pile is empty.
hint.halve3: Check it when you are done: does your answer, doubled, give you back {n}?
hint.group2: Fill one group completely before you start the next.
hint.group3: When nothing is left, count the groups — not the counters.
hint.meaning1: Read it again, slowly. The two numbers in it are telling you different kinds of thing.
hint.meaningSize: “Shared between” gives the groups. What is missing is each share.
hint.meaningCount: “Groups of” gives the size. What is missing is how many groups.
hint.lookSize: You are looking for the size of one share.
hint.lookCount: You are looking for the number of shares.
hint.equation1: The number you started with comes first.
hint.equation2: You started with {n}, so the sentence starts with {n}.
hint.onePlate1: There is only one plate. Nobody else is sharing.
hint.onePlate2: Nothing is being shared away, so everything stays where it is.
hint.same1: Count the plates. Now count the counters.
hint.same2: There is exactly one counter for every plate, so each plate gets one.
hint.zero1: Look for the plates. How many are there?
hint.zero2: There is nowhere to put them. A share you cannot start has no answer at all.
hint.nothing1: There is nothing in the pile to share.
hint.nothing2: The plates stay empty, however many plates there are.
hint.leftover1: Go round again while every plate can still have one.
hint.leftover3: What is left over goes in the box, not on a plate.

tray.notEnough: Stop when there are not enough left to give one to every plate.
tray.zeroPlates: Zero plates is not somewhere to put them. Look again at the question.
tray.meaningRight: Yes — that is the part the question leaves out.
tray.meaningWrong: Look at what the sentence already tells you.
tray.cannotRight: Right. There is nowhere to put them, so there is no answer.
tray.cannotWrong: There are plates here. It can be done — work it out.
tray.equationWrong: Which number did you start with?
tray.leftoverLabel: Leftover box, holding {count}. Put one in.
tray.takeLeftover: Take one back out of the leftover box
tray.inEachOne: How many go in each one?

printed.impossibleAnswer: No — there is nowhere to put them.
printed.meaning: What is the question asking for?   how many in each / how many groups
printed.ring: Ring groups of {d}. How many groups?
printed.leftover: Share these between {d} plates. How many each, and how many left over?
printed.share: Share these between {d} plates. How many on each?

method.group1: Ring the same number of them at a time, as the question says.
method.group2: Keep going while there are enough left for a whole ring.
method.group3: Count the rings, not the counters.
method.leftover1: Give one to each plate, then go round again.
method.leftover3: What is left over is not on a plate. Write it separately.
method.share1: Give one to each plate, then start again at the first.
method.share2: Keep going until they are all shared out.
method.share3: Count what is on one plate.

strategy.title: Which Way?
strategy.prompt: {n} ÷ {d}. Which way would you do it?

halve.label: Halve it, maybe more than once
halve.whyThrice: Dividing by {d} is halving three times.

known-fact.label: Use a times-table fact
known-fact.why: {d} × {q} = {n} is a fact you already know.

place-split.label: Split it by place value
place-split.why: Every place of {n} divides by {d} on its own.

chunk.label: Take away big chunks
chunk.why: The answer is big, so take away tens of {d}s at a time.

scale.label: Cancel the zeros first
scale.why: A zero on each side cancels, and what is left is much smaller.

written.label: Use the written method
written.why: It always works, and this one is big enough to be worth writing out.

strategy.doesNotSuit: That one does not suit these numbers. Look at them again.
strategy.hint1: Look at the numbers before you look at the choices.
strategy.hint2: Is it a number you can halve by? Do all the places divide?
strategy.hint3: More than one way is right. Pick the one these numbers suit.
strategy.method1: Look at the numbers before you look at the choices.
strategy.method2: Ask whether the divisor is one you can halve by, and whether every place divides.
strategy.method3: More than one way can be right. Pick one that suits these numbers.
